M7.4 2 km SE of San José del Palmar, Colombia

What was published about the M7.4 earthquake of 10 August 2026, and what the University of Houston team acquired and did in support of the EEFIT field mission. Each item was released by a named person.

Overview3,893 acquisitions · 1,622 footprints

Every satellite and aerial acquisition the mission catalogued: where each image falls against the mission places, and when it was taken against the earthquake and the field mission (15 Sep–26 Sep). Below it, when each agency delivered products. Outlines show what an image covers, not what it shows. The damage-product layer draws the extent each released product covers (a Copernicus EMS area of interest, or the bounding box of the places it names), never the damage itself; the popup links to the producer.

The map needs the Leaflet library, which did not load here. The timeline and the table below carry the same acquisitions.

Acknowledgements

The University of Houston provided remote sensing support to the EEFIT Colombia 2026 field mission, at the request of Arup. Field assessments were collected by the EEFIT field team between 15 and 26 September 2026.

Satellite products and data are courtesy of USGS, Copernicus EMS, the International Charter Space and Major Disasters, ESA (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2), NASA and ISRO (NISAR), the Alaska Satellite Facility, the Vantor Open Data Program, Planet, Microsoft AI for Good, UNOSAT, IGAC and OpenAerialMap. Commercial SAR imagery was provided by Umbra.

Credits

Compiled by the Milillo Lab at the University of Houston with AGENT_RECON, in remote support of the EEFIT Colombia 2026 field mission. Products and data belong to their producers and are linked at source. Every item carries its id and names the file it was read from, on the line under each card.
